content.text:
View A: The model represents a green circle in the upper location that is currently dominant and readily available. The other three objects are present but unattended: a red triangle at right, a blue square at lower, and a yellow cross at left; each is much less likely to be selected now. Access reliability for the upper green circle is moderate now and declines with one or two intervening shifts; the unattended objects show varying recoverability (the blue square is relatively more recoverable than the red triangle and yellow cross) but all decline with further steps.

View B: The model represents a green triangle at upper (currently dominant), a red circle at right, a blue square at lower (mostly square), and a yellow cross at left. The upper green triangle is strongly attended and most available; the others are largely unattended with limited immediate availability and decreasing recoverability after one or two steps.

Controllability: In both views, commands mainly reinforce the current focus. In A each command tends to keep attention on whichever location is already selected. In B commands almost always drive attention back to the upper location. Thus the system has limited ability to reallocate attention away from the currently dominant upper items.
